notes: S124-01. Scan124 is author page61 with separate pencil123. The inventory covers the opening paragraph, canceled formula, four numbered items, prose, all seven connections of (195), and both marginal numbers. The count of19 main writing baselines includes the four descriptive baselines in (193) and three diagram object rows, but excludes the two marginal numbers. The whole page and native halves were viewed once, followed by all15 saved crops.

S124-02. The manuscript calls the two objects in (193) inverse images of T_d and T_{d'}, describes their ranks, and announces a canonical surjective hom called tautological. These assertions are reported from the page, without an independent proof of the construction or surjectivity. This describes the first reader’s scope; the root’s conditional finite-coordinate check is recorded separately below.

S124-03. The manuscript says the morphism becomes a projection of an integer lattice onto a partial product selected by a d'-element part of I_d. The final identity has a single wavy stroke above a straight bar. No external definition of the underlying objects or proof of the asserted identification was supplied or reconstructed.

S124-04. The three high index clusters were checked individually. The first in (193) has several intersecting strokes, the second is a smaller angular cluster, and the upper group label in (195) has another compact high cluster. Their star-like readings remain local uncertainties; neither recurring notation nor mathematical need was used to turn them into bare d or simple d'.

S124-05. All six decorated D occurrences have distinct stems and dots: two in the prose product, the lower base of the raised P argument, the D after the equivalence sign, and the upper-right and middle-left diagram objects. Separately, the final factor of the prose product is plainly D_{d'}, with no extra d or comma inserted.

S124-06. A source/target check of the written product D^!_d times over D_d with D_{d'} finds that this page supplies no map from D_{d'} to D_d. Its diagram instead supplies a correspondence object D_{d,d'} with maps to both bases. H suggests that latter object as a correction, but the ink in the last factor is the shorter D_{d'}, which remains. This is a local notation/type check, not a proof that the construction is impossible.

S124-07. Diagram(195) has six object positions and seven connections: four clear headed connections, two shafts with one-sided terminal turns, and the headless lower-left diagonal. The lower-left S_d label lies inside the diamond. The (I_d) argument is physically raised; raisebox preserves placement without asserting an exponent. The source P form is read from its bowl and returning strokes, not supplied from a power-set interpretation.

S124-08. Both short display connectors have transverse terminal caps, copied with inline TikZ. The low separator in the right T expression of (194) is a dot rather than the long comma drawn in the left expression. Neither feature is silently standardized according to the intended map.

S124-09. The canceled formula before (193) has a clear lower d and lower-right D_{d,d'}, but the capital is obscured by the diagonal cancellation. The initial s of s’identifie is heavily retraced yet readable; no recoverable older letter is isolated, so no invented canceled letter is added. C contains no insertion macros on this page, and no separate insertion leader is seen.

S124-10. The prose abbreviations are hom twice and ens without terminal points, and can. with a point. H lengthens hom to homom. and reads cart. for can.; both witnesses add points after hom. Quotation marks are paired high ticks. The outer parenthesis opened by cf has no closing parenthesis supplied at the end of the diagram or following prose.

S124-11. M1266, M1267 and M1268 remain undecided with the visible high clusters retained; M1269 receives a literal geometric third reading, with its directional interpretation still open. The unindexed canceled-capital doubt is also retained. H’s explanatory notes were not treated as source text; its note about the canceled Z was used as its reading of that source element, and actual omitted pencil123 receives an omission row.

MC124-R. In the written coordinate model, restriction r_J: Z^I -> Z^J to a d′-element subset is surjective: extension by zero is a right inverse, and the kernel is Z^{I minus J}. For any permutation sigma, evaluating at sigma(j) gives r_(sigma J)(sigma v)(sigma j)=v(j)=sigma(r_J v)(sigma j), so the maps are equivariant as the chosen subset varies. This checks the local projection model conditionally on the manuscript identifications; it proves neither the global descent nor a repaired reading of the visible indices or fibre product. See review/mathematical_checks.md, MC124-R.
